title: 2022 HMMT November Guts Problem 2
statement: The English alphabet, which has 26 letters, is randomly permuted. Let \(p_{1}\) be the probability that \(\mathrm{AB}, \mathrm{CD}\), and EF all appear as contiguous substrings. Let \(p_{2}\) be the probability that ABC and DEF both appear as contiguous substrings. Compute \(\frac{p_{1}}{p_{2}}\).

solutions.text: There are 23! ways to arrange the alphabet such that AB, CD, and EF all appear as contiguous substrings: treat each of these pairs of letters as a single merged symbol, which leaves 23 symbols to permute. Similarly, there are 22! ways to arrange the alphabet such that ABC and DEF both appear as contiguous substrings. Thus, \(p_{1}=23!/ 26!\) and \(p_{2}=22!/ 26!\), so the answer is \(23!/ 22!=23\).
